activity_context.topic_title: The Curvature of a Plane Curve

feedback.problem: Find the curvature of the curve $y={x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}$ at $x=-1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(x)$ of a plane curve $y=y(x)$ is given by

$$
κ(x)=\frac{|{y}^{″}(x)|}{(1+[{y}^{′}(x)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${y}^{′}(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =3{x}^{2}-4x,\, & {y}^{″}(x) & =6x-4\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(x) & =\frac{|6x-4|}{{[1+{(3{x}^{2}-4x)}^{2}]}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(-1) & =\frac{|6(-1)-4|}{{(1+{(3(-1)^{2}-4(-1))}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{|-10|}{{(1+{7}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{10}{{(50)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{10}{50\sqrt{50}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{50}.\end{aligned}
$$
